definition: Money a business owes its suppliers for goods or services already received.
example: The studio records the unpaid printing invoice in accounts payable.
wordNotes: Accounting phrase: accounts are records; payable means due to be paid.

definition: Money customers owe a business for sales already made on credit.
example: Our accounts receivable includes a client invoice due next month.
wordNotes: Accounting phrase: receivable describes money expected to be collected.

definition: Recording revenue when earned and expenses when incurred, even when cash moves later.
example: We earned the fee in June and recorded it in June, although payment arrived in July.
wordNotes: Accrual is formed from accrue, meaning to accumulate.

definition: A resource a business owns or controls that can provide economic benefit.
example: A camera owned by the studio is an asset.
wordNotes: Business noun; the plural is assets.

definition: A statement showing assets, liabilities, and owners’ equity at a particular date.
example: The balance sheet shows what the company owns and owes on December 31.
wordNotes: Compound phrase: a sheet displaying financial balances.

definition: Keeping organized records of financial transactions.
example: Weekly bookkeeping helps us find missing receipts before month-end.
wordNotes: Compound of book and keeping, referring to maintaining records.

definition: A plan for expected income and spending over a period.
example: Our launch budget sets aside money for hosting and promotion.
wordNotes: Used as a noun for the plan and a verb for making it.

definition: Money or other resources used to start, operate, or grow a business.
example: The founders contributed capital to buy equipment.
wordNotes: From Latin capitalis, related to caput, meaning head; modern business meanings developed later.

definition: Recording income when cash is received and expenses when cash is paid.
example: Under cash accounting, we record the payment when it reaches the bank.
wordNotes: Accounting phrase describing timing based on cash movement.

definition: The movement of money into and out of a business over time.
example: A profitable company can still struggle if its cash flow cannot cover bills today.
wordNotes: Compound phrase: cash moves, or flows, through a business.

definition: The direct costs assigned to the goods sold in a period.
example: The mug seller subtracts cost of goods sold to calculate gross profit.
wordNotes: Descriptive accounting phrase; what counts depends on the business and accounting rules.

definition: The owners’ financial interest in a business; on a balance sheet, assets minus liabilities.
example: After subtracting liabilities from assets, the remaining amount is owners’ equity.
wordNotes: Historically related to fairness; this entry covers the accounting and ownership meaning.

definition: A cost recognized as part of operating a business or earning revenue.
example: We record the monthly software subscription as an expense.
wordNotes: Business noun; to expense an item means to recognize a cost under applicable accounting rules.

definition: An estimate of future results based on assumptions and available information.
example: Our sales forecast uses last year’s figures and this year’s planned launches.
wordNotes: Compound of fore, meaning ahead, and cast; forecasts are estimates, not promises.

definition: Revenue minus cost of goods sold, before other expenses are deducted.
example: Selling a product for $40 with $15 in assigned goods costs produces $25 gross profit.
wordNotes: Gross signals an amount before later deductions in this context.

definition: A statement summarizing revenue, expenses, and profit or loss over a period.
example: The income statement shows the quarter’s operating results.
wordNotes: Descriptive phrase; unlike a balance sheet, it covers a span of time.

definition: A document requesting payment and describing the goods or services supplied.
example: We send an invoice after completing the agreed website milestone.
wordNotes: Business noun; invoice can also be a verb meaning to bill a customer.

definition: An obligation a business owes to another party.
example: An unpaid equipment loan is a liability.
wordNotes: Formed from liable and the noun ending -ity.

definition: A profit amount expressed as a share of revenue; name the type of profit used.
example: A $20 gross profit on $100 revenue is a 20 percent gross margin.
wordNotes: This is the financial meaning; the same word can mean an edge or boundary.

definition: The amount left after the relevant expenses are subtracted from revenue.
example: The business earns net profit after deducting its costs and taxes as reported.
wordNotes: Net describes an amount after deductions.

definition: Income from a business’s sales or other operating activities before expenses are subtracted.
example: Selling ten $50 lessons generates $500 in sales revenue.
wordNotes: Business noun; revenue is not the same as profit or cash received.

definition: Current assets minus current liabilities, a measure related to short-term financial capacity.
example: We review working capital before taking on a large order.
wordNotes: Accounting compound: working points to day-to-day business activity.

definition: For a loan, paying down principal through scheduled payments over time.
example: The loan’s amortization schedule separates interest and principal in each payment.
wordNotes: Noun formed from amortize; it also has a separate accounting meaning for certain assets.

definition: A yearly measure of borrowing cost that can include interest and certain fees under the applicable rules.
example: We compare annual percentage rates and total repayment amounts before choosing a loan.
wordNotes: Descriptive phrase; the method and included costs depend on the credit product and rules.

definition: An asset pledged to secure a borrowing obligation.
example: The lender may take specified collateral if the borrower defaults under the agreement.
wordNotes: Business noun; collateral also has other meanings outside lending.

definition: Money or another obligation owed to someone else.
example: The company uses a repayment plan to manage its debt.
wordNotes: Business noun; the written b is silent.

definition: Payments required to cover a debt’s principal and interest over a period.
example: We include monthly debt service in the cash forecast.
wordNotes: Compound phrase: servicing debt means making required payments.

definition: Funding awarded for a specified purpose under eligibility and use conditions, usually without ordinary loan repayment.
example: The applicant checks permitted expenses before applying for a grant.
wordNotes: Used as a noun for the award and a verb for giving it.

definition: The percentage charged for borrowing or earned on certain balances over a stated period.
example: We ask whether the interest rate is fixed or variable.
wordNotes: Descriptive finance phrase; it does not alone show every borrowing cost.

definition: An arrangement allowing borrowing up to an approved limit under agreed terms.
example: The business draws on its line of credit when cash timing is uneven.
wordNotes: Lending phrase; available credit depends on the agreement and outstanding balance.

definition: Money borrowed with an agreement to repay it under specified terms.
example: The owner compares the loan’s repayment schedule and fees.
wordNotes: Business noun; loan is also used as a verb meaning to lend.

definition: The amount borrowed or still owed on a loan, separate from interest.
example: Extra approved payments can reduce the remaining principal.
wordNotes: From Latin principalis, meaning first or chief; do not confuse principal with principle.

definition: A provider’s process for assessing risk and deciding whether to offer financing or insurance and on what terms.
example: The lender reviews records during underwriting before making a decision.
wordNotes: Formed from underwrite; the modern process is more than signing a document.

definition: Building a business mainly with the founders’ resources and operating income rather than outside investment.
example: We begin bootstrapping with a small service offer and reinvest the earnings.
wordNotes: A metaphor based on bootstraps; not a literal promise of growth without resources.

definition: A description of how a business creates value, delivers it, and earns enough to operate.
example: Our business model combines client services and digital products.
wordNotes: Compound phrase; a revenue model covers only the earning portion.

definition: A written description of the business, market, operations, goals, and financial assumptions.
example: We revise the business plan after learning what customers will pay for.
wordNotes: Descriptive compound; useful plans change as evidence improves.

definition: A meaningful strength that helps a business compete and serve customers better than alternatives.
example: Clear instructional design is part of our competitive advantage.
wordNotes: Descriptive business phrase; the advantage must matter to the customer.

definition: Learning about potential customers’ needs and behavior through direct investigation.
example: Customer discovery interviews reveal which problem people already try to solve.
wordNotes: Startup phrase describing learning, not merely collecting compliments.

definition: A specific item or result a project must produce.
example: A tested mobile homepage is one deliverable in the project agreement.
wordNotes: From deliver with -able; used as a noun for the thing to be delivered.

definition: A person who organizes a venture and takes on its business risks.
example: The entrepreneur tests a small offer before investing in a larger launch.
wordNotes: Borrowed from French entrepreneur, associated with undertaking an enterprise.

definition: A measure chosen to track progress toward an important objective.
example: Qualified inquiry count is a key performance indicator for this campaign.
wordNotes: An expanded acronym; not every available metric is a key indicator.

definition: A significant point or completed stage in a project.
example: Approval of the first prototype is our next milestone.
wordNotes: A metaphor from markers showing distance along a road.

definition: A deliberately limited version used to test a key assumption with real users.
example: Our minimum viable product tests one useful workflow before adding more features.
wordNotes: Expanded acronym; viable does not mean careless, unsafe, or unfinished in essential ways.

definition: A statement of an organization’s present purpose and who it serves.
example: Our mission explains why the learning studio exists.
wordNotes: Organization noun; mission concerns purpose, while vision concerns a desired future.

definition: A substantial change in business direction based on what has been learned.
example: We pivot from a broad app to one focused scheduling tool.
wordNotes: A movement word used as a business metaphor for changing direction.

definition: The agreed boundaries of work, including what is included and excluded.
example: The project scope includes five pages and one contact form.
wordNotes: Business use of a word meaning extent or range.

definition: A person or group affected by a project or able to influence it.
example: Learners and the training manager are stakeholders in the course redesign.
wordNotes: Compound of stake, meaning an interest, and holder.

definition: A clear explanation of the useful benefit an offer provides to a specific customer.
example: Our value proposition promises easier team organization, then shows how.
wordNotes: Business phrase; a claim needs supporting evidence.

definition: A description of the future an organization wants to help create.
example: The team’s vision gives long-term direction without replacing a practical plan.
wordNotes: Organization use of a word also associated with seeing.

definition: A comparison of two versions to learn which performs better on a defined measure.
example: We run an A/B test on two headlines with comparable audiences.
wordNotes: Letter-based label: A and B name the two versions.

definition: The identity, associations, and expectations people connect with a business or offer.
example: Consistent design and reliable service strengthen the brand.
wordNotes: Business noun and verb; a logo is one part of a brand.

definition: A clear invitation telling someone what useful step to take next.
example: The call to action invites visitors to request a project discussion.
wordNotes: Expanded acronym; effective actions match the reader’s need.

definition: Clicks divided by impressions, usually expressed as a percentage.
example: Ten clicks from one thousand impressions produce a one percent click-through rate.
wordNotes: Compound phrase naming a ratio; it does not measure sales by itself.

definition: Creating and sharing useful material to attract and support a relevant audience.
example: Our content marketing answers common questions before presenting a service.
wordNotes: Marketing compound; useful content still needs a clear audience and purpose.

definition: A desired action completed by a visitor or customer, such as a signup or purchase.
example: Submitting a qualified inquiry counts as a conversion for this page.
wordNotes: Business use of convert; define the action before measuring it.

definition: Conversions divided by the relevant visits, users, or opportunities, expressed as a percentage.
example: Five inquiries from one hundred visits give a five percent visit-based conversion rate.
wordNotes: Descriptive ratio; always state which denominator you used.

definition: Relevant acquisition spending divided by new customers acquired in a defined period.
example: We compare customer acquisition cost with what each customer contributes.
wordNotes: Expanded acronym; included costs and time period should be clearly stated.

definition: The practices and systems used to organize customer information and interactions.
example: Customer relationship management keeps follow-up notes in one shared system.
wordNotes: Expanded acronym; CRM can mean the approach or the software supporting it.

definition: Observable interactions with content or an experience, such as comments, saves, or meaningful use.
example: We track engagement but also check whether visitors achieve their goals.
wordNotes: From engage with the noun ending -ment; platforms define measurements differently.

definition: A recorded display of content or an advertisement under a platform’s counting rules.
example: One person may generate several impressions by seeing an ad repeatedly.
wordNotes: Marketing noun; impressions are not the same as unique people reached.

definition: A potential customer who has shown some relevant interest or meets a defined prospecting criterion.
example: The project inquiry becomes a lead for the studio.
wordNotes: In this business meaning, lead rhymes with seed, not the metal lead.

definition: An estimate of the value a customer relationship contributes over its duration.
example: We calculate lifetime value using stated assumptions about retention and margin.
wordNotes: Business phrase; revenue-based and profit-based calculations differ.

definition: The unique audience reached without paying to promote that particular content.
example: Helpful posts can build organic reach, although visibility is not guaranteed.
wordNotes: Marketing meaning of organic; it does not mean chemical-free content.

definition: The number of distinct people or accounts exposed to content under a platform’s measurement method.
example: The campaign reached fewer people than its total impression count.
wordNotes: Common word used as a measurement; platforms may estimate it differently.

definition: A model of stages people may pass through from awareness to a purchase.
example: Our sales funnel connects useful teaching with a relevant service inquiry.
wordNotes: Metaphor based on a funnel; real journeys are not always linear.

definition: Improving a site so search systems can understand it and people can find useful, relevant content.
example: Our search engine optimization includes clear titles and accessible pages.
wordNotes: Expanded acronym; SEO does not guarantee rankings.

definition: The specific people an offer or message is designed to serve.
example: Our target audience includes small teams needing practical AI workflows.
wordNotes: Descriptive phrase; useful audience definitions include needs, not just age.

definition: Computing methods used for tasks such as prediction, language generation, and pattern recognition.
example: We use artificial intelligence to draft options, then review the result.
wordNotes: Expanded acronym; capabilities depend on the particular system and task.

definition: An application programming interface: a defined way for software components to interact.
example: The app uses an API to request approved information from another system.
wordNotes: Initialism spoken letter by letter.

definition: Using systems to carry out steps with less repeated manual work.
example: Automation sends a reminder when an approved task reaches its deadline.
wordNotes: Noun formed from automate; automated work can still require human oversight.

definition: A collection of information organized for analysis or another defined purpose.
example: The dataset contains only the fields needed for the approved task.
wordNotes: Compound of data and set.

definition: AI systems that produce outputs such as text, images, audio, or code from learned patterns and inputs.
example: Generative AI drafts a lesson outline that a teacher revises.
wordNotes: Generative means producing; AI abbreviates artificial intelligence.

definition: In AI discussions, a plausible-sounding output that is inaccurate, invented, or unsupported.
example: The assistant’s invented source is an AI hallucination.
wordNotes: A metaphor borrowed from a different clinical meaning; it is not a diagnosis of software.

definition: A process that includes human judgment or action at defined points.
example: We keep a human in the loop before sending AI-written customer messages.
wordNotes: Process metaphor: the loop is the sequence of system activity.

definition: Connecting systems so information or actions can work together.
example: The integration connects approved form responses with a customer record.
wordNotes: From integrate with the noun ending -ion.

definition: A model trained on large amounts of language-related data to produce or analyze language.
example: A large language model drafts possible replies but does not guarantee their truth.
wordNotes: Expanded acronym; language fluency and factual accuracy are different qualities.

definition: Methods that learn patterns from data to support predictions or other tasks.
example: Machine learning helps classify support requests using past examples.
wordNotes: Expanded acronym; learning here describes a computational training process.

definition: The instructions, questions, and context supplied to an AI system for a task.
example: Our prompt states the audience, goal, constraints, and review criteria.
wordNotes: Computing use of a word meaning to cue or encourage a response.

definition: An early model used to explore, explain, or test a design.
example: The clickable prototype tests navigation before the full build.
wordNotes: From Greek elements associated with first and model; prototypes can vary in fidelity.

definition: Checking a claim or result against suitable evidence or requirements.
example: Verification catches the draft’s incorrect dates before publication.
wordNotes: Noun formed from verify; the check must suit the consequence of an error.

definition: An ordered set of steps, responsibilities, inputs, and outputs used to complete work.
example: Our workflow shows who reviews a draft before it is published.
wordNotes: Compound of work and flow.

definition: A step or constraint that limits how much work a process can complete.
example: The approval queue is the bottleneck, not the writing speed.
wordNotes: Metaphor from a bottle’s narrow neck.

definition: A condition or task that another task relies on.
example: Final editing has a dependency on receiving the approved script.
wordNotes: From depend with the noun ending -ency.

definition: A cycle in which results inform changes to the next action or version.
example: Learner responses create a feedback loop for improving the course.
wordNotes: Compound phrase describing information returning to guide a process.

definition: A repeated cycle of making, testing, and improving something.
example: Each iteration uses evidence from the previous test.
wordNotes: From iterate, meaning to repeat.

definition: A defined measurement used to describe or monitor something.
example: Completion time is one metric, but accuracy matters too.
wordNotes: Measurement noun; a metric becomes a KPI only when tied to an important objective.

definition: Documented instructions for performing a recurring task consistently.
example: The standard operating procedure includes the reviewer and exception route.
wordNotes: Expanded acronym; a useful procedure describes what to do when normal steps fail.

definition: Designing so people with different abilities can perceive, understand, and use an experience.
example: Keyboard access and readable contrast improve accessibility.
wordNotes: From accessible with -ity; accessibility is more than visual appearance.

definition: A way of gathering evidence about learning or performance.
example: The assessment asks learners to apply the skill in a realistic scenario.
wordNotes: From assess with -ment; an assessment should match the intended skill.

definition: Planning learning experiences around learner needs, goals, practice, and evidence of progress.
example: Instructional design connects the course objective with the activity and assessment.
wordNotes: Compound phrase; it covers learning decisions as well as presentation.

definition: A clear statement of what a learner should be able to do after learning.
example: The learning objective asks learners to compare two options using evidence.
wordNotes: Education phrase; observable actions make the intended result clearer.

definition: A design approach that adapts layout to different screens and conditions.
example: Responsive design keeps the form usable on a narrow phone screen.
wordNotes: Web design phrase; adaptation should preserve usability, not just shrink text.

definition: How effectively, efficiently, and satisfactorily intended users can complete tasks in context.
example: We test usability by watching someone complete a real task.
wordNotes: From usable with -ity; attractive appearance alone does not establish usability.

definition: The speed at which a business uses cash; specify whether you mean gross spending or net cash loss.
example: We track net burn rate to understand how long our current cash can last.
wordNotes: Business metaphor: burn refers to using cash, not literal fire.

definition: An informal way to describe an opportunity that seems easier to achieve than alternatives.
example: Fixing a broken signup link is low-hanging fruit compared with a full redesign.
wordNotes: Metaphor from fruit that is easy to reach; easy still needs to be worthwhile.

definition: To make a noticeable change in an important result.
example: We ask whether the new feature will move the needle on customer success.
wordNotes: Informal metaphor from a gauge’s moving indicator.

definition: A central measure chosen to reflect the value a product delivers and guide decisions.
example: The team chooses a north star metric and checks supporting measures too.
wordNotes: Metaphor based on a guiding star; no single measure captures everything.

definition: An estimate of how long available cash can support operations at an assumed net burn rate.
example: If cash is $20,000 and monthly net burn stays $2,000, estimated runway is ten months.
wordNotes: Business metaphor from the distance available before takeoff; assumptions can change.

definition: Uncontrolled growth in project work without appropriate changes to time, cost, or agreement.
example: Extra features become scope creep when nobody updates the agreed plan.
wordNotes: Project metaphor: creep describes gradual, sometimes unnoticed expansion.

definition: Having a personal stake in a decision’s outcome.
example: The partner has skin in the game because their own resources are at risk.
wordNotes: Informal idiom; use clearer wording when the audience may not know it.

definition: A combined effect that is better than the parts working separately, when evidence supports the claim.
example: Shared research creates synergy if both teams can use it effectively.
wordNotes: From Greek synergos, meaning working together; it is often used vaguely in business.

definition: Organizing, interpreting, and reporting financial information about a business.
example: Accounting turns transaction records into statements that support decisions.
wordNotes: Formed from account and -ing; bookkeeping is one part of accounting.

definition: The amount by which revenue exceeds the costs included in a stated calculation.
example: We specify gross or net profit so everyone knows which costs were deducted.
wordNotes: Business noun; profit can also be a verb meaning to gain a benefit.

definition: The amount added to cost to set a selling price, often expressed as a percentage of cost.
example: A $10 cost with a 50 percent markup gives a $15 selling price, before any other charges.
wordNotes: Compound of mark and up; markup uses cost as its base, while margin uses revenue.
